source: CDCR Division of Rehabilitative Programs — Grant Programs page and RFA documents

grants.name: RIGHT Grant 4.0
grants.fullName: Rehabilitative Investment Grants for Healing and Transformation (RIGHT) Grant 4.0
grants.howAwarded: Every eligible organization gets qualifying points; the total is divided by all points awarded, so each point is worth the same amount.
eligibility: Community-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit in good standing, or fiscally sponsored by one
Provided rehabilitative programming inside a CDCR institution in at least 2 of the 5 years before applying
Currently providing an existing rehabilitative program
Programs do not need to be RAC approved (FAQ 71)
points: Budget under $250,000: 1 point · $250,000–$500,000: 2 points · over $500,000: 3 points
+0.5 for programming at an underserved institution (Attachment A, red font)
+0.5 for a program in a language other than English
At most two half-points (+1.0); maximum 4 points per organization
documents: IRS 501(c)(3) determination letter (or fiscal sponsor's) and fiscal sponsor agreement if any
Annual budget for FY 2024-25 and FY 2025-26, one PDF each
STD 204 Payee Data Record (STD 205 optional) and Supplement Payee Data Record
Office of Business Services forms 1000, 1500 and 1510
Certificate of Insurance; Workers' Compensation exemption if applicable; Contractor Certification Clauses
Program Summary (max 2 pages) and Attachment A – Institution Locations & Populations
notes: The packet includes a Generative AI (GenAI) reporting form: disclose any AI use in preparing the application.
Grantees submit an annual report within 60 days after each fiscal year.

programSummary.limit: At most 2 pages; not scored, but required.
mustInclude: The institution(s)/location(s) where the existing program is delivered
How the program specifically benefits the incarcerated population there
The type of program: correspondence, in-person, or hybrid
Program goals and objectives for participants
The resources needed to deliver it (space, equipment)
programSummary.ifNonEnglish: Name the language(s), how it is delivered (bilingual facilitators, certified interpreters, translated materials, etc.), any link between the language and the institution, and the organization's experience and capacity to deliver in that language.
